clue.text: Schemer, drunk in charge, in serious trouble?

indicators.note: the drunk and in-charge pieces are placed in the middle of the word for serious trouble

parts.note: being in deep poo is slang for serious trouble
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A tipsy official with responsibilities finds himself in a real mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a political operator, someone who manoeuvres and plots for advantage.

clue.text: Taken as 23, serving also to separate sons and daughters

parts.note: to serve under someone, so serving can mean under

indicators.note: the word for also is put between the sons and daughters abbreviations, keeping them apart

parts.note: S is the genealogy abbreviation for son
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter
too means also

explanation.surface: A rule taken for granted, used to keep boys and girls apart at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to the answer at 23-across, READ, so the definition is the idiom 'taken as read'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken as read is assumed or tacitly agreed, without needing to be said.

clue.text: To an alpine resort to find an Italian

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: Travelling to a ski resort in the Alps in search of an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday destination after 'alpine', but read as re-sort it is the anagram signal on TO AN ALPINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Naples, the southern Italian city, is called by this demonym.

clue.text: Husband in vehicle supplies fish — daily!

indicators.note: the husband abbreviation goes inside the word for a vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A married man in a van delivers fresh fish every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a bonus second definition: a daily is a British cleaning lady, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: The char is a trout-like freshwater fish of cold northern lakes.

clue.text: Shock for commentator — runner coming into form

indicators.note: what a commentator says is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: A commentator is stunned as an athlete hits top form.
explanation.walkthrough: A hare's resting place is called its form, so the runner 'coming into form' is the animal returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: This fast long-eared animal is a runner, and its nest in the grass is called a form.

clue.text: Language doctor up in posh university

indicators.note: the reversed doctor goes inside the two U letters

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A medic going up to an exclusive university.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Youngster beneath wee vessel shows spirit

indicators.note: in a down entry, the youngster word is written below the vessel word

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot, a vessel for wee
a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: A teenager under a small boat proves full of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like Scots for small, but the vessel is one for wee: a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Poteen is an Irish illicitly distilled spirit, traditionally made from potatoes.

clue.text: Brief recovery of dead cat — black one!

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
one refers back to the cat: the ounce, or snow leopard, is a big cat

explanation.surface: A dead black cat briefly stirs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'dead cat bounce' is a stock-market term for a short-lived recovery in a falling price.
explanation.definitionFit: Traders call a temporary rally in a collapsing share price a dead cat bounce.

clue.text: Last at Crucible to come in had chance for clearance

indicators.note: the final letter is to enter the word had

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word Crucible is taken

parts.note: room, as in room for doubt, means scope or chance

explanation.surface: A snooker player at the Crucible came in last but had a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible is a Sheffield theatre that hosts the World Snooker Championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the clearance above, the space between something and the ceiling.

clue.text: Cover the skin

definitions.meaning: to cover something is to conceal it

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means conceal from view; as a noun it is an animal's skin.

clue.text: Language removed by editor after power abused

indicators.note: the language, removed and editor pieces come after the power abbreviation

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland
cut means removed, as from a text

explanation.surface: Words struck out by an editor after authority was misused.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone persecuted has been harassed or ill-treated, abused over a period.

clue.text: Young lady lives in Marks & Spencer?

indicators.note: the word for lives goes inside the store abbreviation

parts.note: M&S is the usual short form of Marks & Spencer, the British department store
is, as in exists or lives

explanation.surface: A girl lives in a department store.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is the title for, and a word for, a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Where lucre's filthy this cleans up!

definitions.text: Where lucre's filthy this cleans up!

parts.words: Where lucre's filthy this cleans up!
parts.note: filthy lucre is dirty money, and the process that cleans it is the washing of criminal proceeds

explanation.surface: Something that tidies up wherever money is dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Money is washed when criminal proceeds are passed through legitimate businesses to hide their origin.

clue.text: Release head departing BBC

indicators.note: the first letter of the nickname leaves

parts.note: Auntie is an affectionate British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: A chief executive leaving the broadcaster is set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo a knot, freeing or releasing what was tied.

clue.text: Having mistaken opinions, cat seizes American in wood

indicators.note: the cat-and-American piece goes inside the word for wood

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber

indicators.note: the cat word holds the American abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat in a forest catches an American visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deluded holds false beliefs firmly despite evidence to the contrary.

clue.text: Android mad to consume black goo is slowing down

indicators.note: the shuffled word swallows the black goo word
mad suggests the letters of the robot word go wild into a new order

parts.note: tar is a black sticky substance

explanation.surface: A crazy robot swallowing black sludge grinds to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Android mad' looks like a description of a robot, but it is the anagram, and its scrambled letters are split by the goo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritardando is a musical direction meaning gradually getting slower.

clue.text: Ultra-conservative parties

parts.note: a do is a party; two of them are needed
the second party, another do

explanation.surface: Hardline right-wing political parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' looks political, but here it is social gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo is an old fogey, someone hopelessly behind the times.

clue.text: Ruin everything

definitions.meaning: to wreck completely, as in writing off a car

explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb for wrecking a car; as a noun, the whole sum of something.

clue.text: Gather food

definitions.meaning: to fold or gather fabric into a pleat
British schoolboy slang for food and sweets

explanation.definitionFit: A pleat gathered in cloth; also old British school slang for snacks and sweets.

clue.text: Shops saying cut certain with this item

parts.note: chains are groups of shops under one owner
a saw is a proverb or saying

explanation.surface: Store groups announce cuts are certain.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorised saw with a toothed chain, which makes any cut certain.

clue.text: Pages wrong about Shakespearean forest produce

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the forest
the letters of the word pages are put wrong, into another order

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: Misprinted pages about a forest in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like a verb but is the noun: garden vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden peas are vegetables, produce grown in a garden.

clue.text: As modernist works in solo after a fashion, one discarded

indicators.note: the trimmed solo word comes after the fashion piece

parts.note: ton means fashion or style, as in bon ton

indicators.note: the letters of the word one are thrown away

parts.note: alone means solo
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Modern composers working alone after a fashion, with one dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Much twentieth-century modernist music abandons any key, having no tonal centre.

clue.text: Examine register

definitions.meaning: to study or pore over a text
to show a measurement, as a meter does

explanation.definitionFit: To peruse a text; also what a gauge does when it shows a figure.

clue.text: Bird grabs hot dog that's rancid, or very dodgy

indicators.note: the bird holds the hot abbreviation inside it

parts.note: the toucan is a big-billed tropical bird
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: rancid suggests the dog has gone off, its letters spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird snatches a hot dog that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch-and-go describes an outcome highly uncertain or precarious.

clue.text: Langley folks love Berlusconi's farewell

parts.note: the CIA is headquartered in Langley, Virginia
love is zero in tennis, looking like O

explanation.surface: Spies send love as an Italian prime minister departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is the Italian goodbye, as Silvio Berlusconi, an Italian prime minister, would say.

clue.text: Once more with sheep — tails docked

indicators.note: both words lose their final letter

parts.note: and means with, plus
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Again working with sheep that have had their tails cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tails docked' applies to both words, so AND loses its D and EWE loses its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means again, afresh, once more.

clue.text: Cheerless Celtic poet sent up

indicators.note: in a down entry, the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: a bard is a poet, especially of Celtic tradition

explanation.surface: A gloomy Welsh poet is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like mockery but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and dreary, lacking cheer.

clue.text: Problem to face in Isaac Newton

indicators.note: the letters are found in the run of the scientist's name

explanation.surface: A difficulty facing the great physicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots on the face are a skin problem, especially for teenagers.

clue.text: Returned without delay to study area — this one's in the US

indicators.note: the word for without delay is read backwards

parts.note: ASAP stands for as soon as possible
a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: Coming back promptly to a study area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This one' refers to the area: Pasadena is an area, a city, in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in California, near Los Angeles.

clue.text: Answer to new clergyman in Peak District

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric

explanation.surface: A response to a new vicar in Derbyshire's national park.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District is an English national park; but the peaks here are the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean means of the Andes, the South American mountain region of high peaks.
